description: Generate a game sprite/asset image. Infer every field from the request: art STYLE, colour PALETTE, asset TYPE, output SIZE and PERSPECTIVE; for characters also facing/pose/bodyType. Leave model out unless the user names one: the server then picks by size (flux2-klein, 1 credit, up to 64 px; gpt-image-2.5, 3 credits, from 96 px). Costs by model: flux2-klein 1, gpt-image-2.5 3, gpt-image-2.6 10 credits (a reference image makes it 2 and uses flux2-klein). ASSET SHEETS: type 'artwork' + model 'gpt-image-2.6' + size 2048 (20 credits) or '4k' (30 credits) draws one big picture holding a whole matching set (e.g. 'nine fantasy RPG items in a grid, clear space between them, plain light background') at full resolution; cut it into one asset per item with extract_parts save_as 'assets' (each cut-out a 1024 sprite). Call it once per request and show the result; ask the user before generating again (each call spends credits). Every image is drawn in exactly one of Voidless's fixed style presets, and the result says which one was used and why. Model 'free' is Voidless Monarch (free), not AI: procedural pixel art drawn by code (free.kind: items, character, props, animals, tiles, creatures, effects, ui, buildings, vehicles, backgrounds, planets, liquids, props3d, character3d, animals3d, items3d, buildings3d, vehicles3d, creatures3d), instant, 0 credits; use it only when the user asks for free or procedural pixel art or a quick placeholder, never by default (options in `free`).

aspect.description: type 'artwork' at size 512, 1024, 2048 or '4k' only: '16:9' for a backdrop, scene or game background (1344x756 at 1024, 672x378 at 512; pixel-art styles come out on a 4 px grid, 672x376 at 512; 2560x1440 at 2048, 3840x2160 at '4k'). Smaller sizes, Retro Diffusion and everything that is not artwork are always 1:1

facing.description: Characters in '2d' or 'isometric': front view or side profile. Side profiles rotate best. Not used for dimension 'top down' (drawn from above whatever the facing), where it is left out

free.description: Only with model 'free': options of Voidless Monarch (free), the procedural generator. generate_image's `size` 16, 24, 32, 48 or 64 is the level of detail of every 2D kind (a sword at 64 is drawn with more detail than at 32, never scaled up); free.size is the same, and wins. Everything is optional and read from the prompt (plain words reach every option: "a wizard with blue hat and green robe holding sword and square face") when left out. A character also takes its parts by name (archetype, skin, hair, hairColor, top, topColor, legs, shoes, cape, headwear, held, offhand, fps...), items material, secondary_color, variant (a shape: kite, curved, flask, buckler, katana...), state (broken, rusty, enchanted, cursed, ancient, pristine, frozen, burning, glowing, poisoned, bloodied, mossy, cracked, gilded, wrapped, charred, wet), pattern (runes, stripes, studded, filigree...), inlay (a gem: ruby, sapphire...), quality (crude, fine, ornate, masterwork), fill (empty, half, full) and columns, props shadow and columns, an animal its species, coat, coat2, pattern, markings, body_size (small x0.75, normal its true size, large x1.33), age, build, mane, horns, saddle, bridle, pack, armor, collar and tack_color, a creature its species, color, color2, pattern, body_size (tiny x0.56, small x0.75, its own true size, large x1.33, huge x1.78, boss at least 100 px tall), eyes, eye_color, mood, spikes, horns, wings, shell, armor and crown, tiles their terrain (grass, dirt, sand, snow, cobble, water, lava, dungeon-wall, castle-brick...), under (the second terrain), top, layout (full, autotile, blob47, variations, single), edge, wear, detail, pieces, animated, frames and color2, an effect its type (fireball, explosion, slash, rain...), element, color, secondary_color, size (16 to 64, the level of detail; 96 too), magnitude, frames (4 to 16), speed, loop, direction (right, left, up... or all), intensity, look (chunky, soft) and trail, UI its type (button, health-bar, panel, dialog-box, inventory-slot, key...), set (a whole kit), theme (wood, stone, metal, paper, glass, scifi, cute, dark), color, accent_color, state (normal, hover, pressed, disabled, on, off), fill (empty to full), size (16 to 64, the level of detail; 8 and 12 too), width, height, corner, border, glyph (play, close, w, space...) and rarity., buildings types (cottage, blacksmith, church, castle, wizard-tower, lighthouse, skyscraper, stone-bridge...), theme (medieval, fantasy, desert, snow, asian, tropical, haunted, modern, scifi, postapoc), wall, wall_color, roof, roof_material, roof_color, trim_color, floors, width, condition (new, worn, ruined, burning, overgrown, snowy), door, windows, sign, chimney, extra, lit, open, view (topdown or side), size (64 to 192: a step of a third from 96 around its true size) and count, a vehicle its type (cart, car, pickup, truck, tank, train-engine, rowboat, galleon, pirate-ship, plane, helicopter, space-fighter, flying-carpet...), color, color2, material, condition (new, rusty, damaged, burning), marking (police, medic, military, pirate, royal, racing, taxi, fire), cargo, lights, view (topdown, side or top), dirs (8, 4 or 1), size (32 to 128: a step of a third from the type's own size around its true length) and animations (still, idle, move, destroyed).

animations.description: character, animals, creatures: what to draw (default still; animals have no jump; a creature has still, idle, move, attack, hurt and death; a vehicle still, idle, move and destroyed)

biome.description: props: the colours and mix of trees, plants and rocks

category.description: props, with no types: a whole group (containers, furniture, village, dungeon, magic, scifi, castle, graveyard, farm, camp, mine, dock, roads, shop, snow, trees, plants, ground, rocks, water, crops, shore) or nature (a mix of what the biome grows)

color.description: items: a colour for every item's main part (red, crimson, teal, navy, brown, gold, silver... or a hex; secondary_color takes the same for the hilt, trim or bottle); props: the thing itself (a red door; the leaves, petals, caps, crystals or stone of a tree, plant or rock), a colour name or a hex

count.description: items, props: how many sprites on the sheet

directions.description: character, animals, creatures, vehicles: only these directions (down, down-right, right, up-right, up, up-left, left, down-left); 3D: how many directions the sheet has, 8, 16 or 32

element.description: items, character: fire, ice, poison, holy, shadow, lightning, arcane, nature, blood

fruit_color.description: props: the fruit, berries or flowers of a bush or tree, a colour name or a hex

growth.description: props: sapling, small, large or giant

heldColor.description: character: what the held item is made of: steel, gold, red, blue, green, purple, black, white, bone, wood or a hex colour

kind.description: What to draw: items (icons and loot), character (an RPG character with directions and animations), props (everything else in a game world: barrels, furniture, dungeon and sci-fi objects, trees, plants and rocks) animals (four-legged animals, from a mouse to a dragon, with directions and animations), creatures (every other enemy and living thing: slimes, bats, birds, insects, snakes, crawlers, fish, plant monsters, constructs, elementals and bosses, with directions and animations) or tiles (a tileset: top-down terrain, floors, liquids and walls with an autotile set, or a side-view platformer ground set with its level pieces; also what type 'tileset' draws), effects (animated strips: projectiles, impacts and explosions, fire, smoke, weather, status marks), ui (HUD parts, panels, buttons, input prompts, or a whole kit), buildings (large structures: houses, shops, farm buildings, churches, castles and towers, fantasy places, lighthouses, big tents, modern and sci-fi buildings, bridges and gates) vehicles (carts, cars, trucks, a tank, trains, boats and ships, planes, a helicopter, spaceships, a flying carpet, with directions and idle, move and destroyed animations), backgrounds (a layered parallax background that scrolls: day, sunset, night, dusk forest, snowy mountains, alien world, desert), planets (a rotating planet, gas giant, star or asteroid, with rings and clouds) or liquids (a seamless looping animated water, lava, acid or waterfall tile); or, in 3D (Voidless Monarch 3D, see mode), items3d (a voxel weapon, gun, hat, crown, helmet, armour, boots, tool, torch, key, book, potion, bag, coin, gem, food…), props3d (furniture, a crate, chest, barrel, sign, fence, lamp post, campfire, statue, gravestone, well, fountain, a tree, palm, bush, flower, mushroom, rock, crystal, cactus…), buildings3d (a house, shop, tavern, tower, castle, windmill, tent, hut, barn, church, lighthouse, bridge, wall, gate) or vehicles3d (a car, truck, bus, tank, bike, train, wagon, plane, helicopter, boat, ship, spaceship, tractor), each as a GLB and a sprite stack, or character3d, animals3d and creatures3d (a rigged voxel knight, wizard, dwarf, goblin… or horse, lion, elephant, dragon… or parrot, owl, snake, shark, spider, slime, ghost…: a skinned, animated GLB and a sprite stack per frame). Every sprite (character, animals, creatures, vehicles, a single item, prop or building, an effect) comes out on a 128x128 canvas, never scaled up: what stands has its lowest pixel on row 112 and is centred across, items and effects are centred, a clear margin of 8 px stays round it (16 on 256), and what does not fit with that margin uses 256x256 (ground row 224) or 512x512 by the same rules; every frame of every animation and direction is on the same canvas at the same place. Animals, creatures, vehicles, props and buildings are drawn at one true scale with the 51 px (1.8 m) character, about 28 px a metre: a cat 14 px (smallest things 12), a wolf 23, a horse 68, an elephant 90, a barrel 28, a car 127 px long, a cottage 170 tall; vehicles stop at 160 px and props and buildings at 416 (a galleon, a castle are smaller than real). Items are icons at their own 16 to 32 px. Tiles, backgrounds, planets, liquids, UI parts and packed sheets of many items, props or buildings keep their own sizes. Default: from type and the prompt

lit.description: props: fires, lamps and screens lit or out (default: the seed decides)

mode.description: Voidless Monarch 3D: '3d' makes a voxel model, handed out as a GLB and a sprite stack (a slice strip and an 8, 16 or 32-direction sheet; the first image is a turntable GIF of the stack, 32 angles at camera 0.7) for fake-3D top-down games: items3d, props3d, buildings3d and vehicles3d (options object, variant (its shape: wizard|top-hat|cowboy… for a hat, katana|rapier… for a sword, pirate|viking|steam for a ship), color, color2, material (items: iron, steel, gold, silver, bronze, wood, stone, bone, crystal, obsidian, leather, cloth, glass; buildings: plaster, wood, log, stone, brick, sandstone), roof_color, wood, metal, leaves, size small|medium|large, directions, squash, step; a thing not made yet gets the closest, and the reply says so) and character3d (a rigged humanoid: archetype, skin, hair, hairColor, headwear, headwearColor, top, topColor, legsColor, cape, capeColor, held, offhand, build (slim, average, broad, child, tall, stocky, huge), beard, ears; 39 classes from knight and wizard to blacksmith, cowboy, astronaut, elf, dwarf, goblin, orc, troll, vampire, demon and golem; a skinned GLB with idle, walk, run and attack, and a sprite stack per frame), animals3d (54 four-legged species, dogs and cats to elephants, crocodiles, frogs, a unicorn, a dragon: species or group, color, color2, pattern, saddle, armor, wings, mane, horns, size; idle, walk and run, a hopper's hop, a winged one's fly) and creatures3d (birds: chicken, duck, crow, owl, parrot, eagle, seagull, penguin, flamingo, peacock, phoenix…; a bat, fish and sharks, snakes, worms and eels, spiders, crabs and scorpions, slimes, a ghost, a flying eye, a mimic: species or group, color, color2, pattern, size small|medium|large|giant; each its own clips: fly and glide, swim, slither, bounce, float…). A thing or creature not made yet gets the closest one, and the reply says so. '2d' keeps it pixel art. Default: from the prompt ('a 3D red car', 'stacked crate', 'voxel house' are 3D)

morph.description: Any kind, 2D and 3D: the composition (read from the prompt when left out: "lizard man", "lizard car", "fire horse", "potion with a lizard face", "centaur archer"). { themes: [concepts, the first strongest: any animal or creature species (lizard, wolf, owl, shark, octopus, spider…), a material (stone, ice, crystal, gold, wood, slime, bone, robot, ghost, lava…), an element (fire, lightning, poison, holy, shadow, arcane) or a style (pirate, steampunk, scifi, candy, royal, viking, spooky, cute…)], body: humanoid | centaur | naga | merfolk | arachne (a person's upper body on a horse, a coil, a fish's tail or a spider), lower: the taur's lower species, head: a species whose head a being has, face: a species whose face goes on a thing, tail, wings (feather, bat, dragon, insect), horns (bull, ram, goat, antlers, demon, unicorn), ears, arms (wings, tentacles, claws), legs (digitigrade, hooves, talons, paws), back (shell, spikes, fins), hat (tricorn, top-hat, crown, wizard-hat…), colors: [main, accent], strength 0.2-1 }. Named hybrids are presets: lizardfolk, kobold, dragonborn, minotaur, centaur, satyr, harpy, birdfolk, catfolk, werewolf, merfolk, naga, arachne, griffin, chimera, pegasus, jackalope, owlbear. Copyrighted characters are never made: their names are dropped and the reply says so.

open.description: props: chests, doors and coffins open or closed (default: the seed decides)

outline.description: colored (default), none, black, white or a hex colour; 3D: true for a dark outline round the stack

palette.description: Draw only in these colours, 2D and 3D: a named palette (pico8, gameboy, nes, endesga32, endesga64, sweetie16, resurrect64, aap64, apollo, pear36, lospec500, steamlords, oil6, twilight5, islandjoy16, fantasy24, zughy32, cga, c64, zxspectrum, 1bit) or hex codes (a list, or one string like "#1a1c2c #5d275d #b13e53"); 2 to 64. Every pixel, outline included, is one of its colours. A palette named in the prompt ("pico-8 knight") or hex codes there work too

rarity.description: items: common, uncommon, rare, epic, legendary or random

save.description: Also save the result to the library (free, private)

scale.description: Scale the returned images up, nearest neighbour (default 1)

seed.description: Same seed and options, same result (default: random)

size.description: 3D: small, medium, large or giant. Sprite px: items 16, 24 or 32; props 16, 32, 48 or 64 (a step of a third from 32 around its true size: 16 x0.75, 48 x1.33, 64 x1.78); tiles 16, 24, 32 or 48; platformer character 48 (the compact body) or 64 (the long-legged one; both on the 128 px canvas) (default: generate_image's size when it is one of these)

species.description: character: human, elf, dwarf, goblin, orc, skeleton, zombie, wolf, cat, lizard, demon, mushroom, robot, ghost, vampire, fairy, angel, slime, bear, fox, rabbit, bird, frog, pig, minotaur, treant, golem, alien, snowman, scarecrow, pumpkin, mummy, imp, ogre, gnome, halfling, fish, insect

state.description: props: broken, mossy, overgrown, snowy, burning or burnt

style.description: Pixel-art look, for every kind (default shaded; bold for a platformer character): flat, handheld (4 greens), 8bit, soft (pastel), dark, bold, 16bit (rich, dithered shadows), 1bit (black and white, dithered), pico8 (a fixed 16-colour palette), nes (3 colours a part from a fixed retro palette), hibit (smooth, no outline) or custom (palette)

theme.description: props: the materials, colours and mix of made things (village, dungeon, royal, haunted, desert, snow, scifi); tiles: the biome or setting (forest, desert, snow, swamp, volcano, cave, dungeon, castle, town, beach, scifi, candy, haunted, farm)

trunk_color.description: props: the trunk, bark or stem of a tree or plant, a colour name or a hex

types.description: items: sword, potion, shield...; props (244 types): barrel, crate, table, pillar, terminal, windmill, cannon, minecart, boat, oak, pine, fruit-tree, bush, rock, flower, wheat, pond...

view.description: character: topdown (3/4 RPG, 8 directions), platformer (side view, right and left) or tall; tiles: topdown or platformer; buildings: topdown or side (the flat front); vehicles: topdown, side or top (straight from above). Default: from the prompt, else from dimension ('2d' platformer, otherwise topdown)

model.description: Only when the user names a model. Left out, the server picks by size: flux2-klein up to 64 px, gpt-image-2.5 from 96 px. 'free' = Voidless Monarch (free): procedural pixel art drawn by code, 0 credits, only when the user asks for free or procedural art.

palette.description: Colour-scheme preset, independent of style. 'none' = the palette the prompt names (e.g. 'in a neon palette', 'endesga 32 knight', 'greyscale'), else the style's own colours. Named palettes (fixed colours, the same as Voidless Monarch's): pico8, gameboy, nes, endesga32, endesga64, sweetie16, resurrect64, aap64, apollo, pear36, lospec500, steamlords, oil6, twilight5, islandjoy16, fantasy24, zughy32, cga, c64, zxspectrum, 1bit (common spellings like 'pico-8', 'game boy', '1-bit' work too). Moods (no fixed colours): black-and-white, retro, vibrant, pastel, neon, earthy, sepia, sunset, ice, dungeon, forest, desert, candy, cyberpunk. Pixel art (32-384 px, or a pixel style) is held to a named palette's exact colours (the ones the art uses most, up to 32; nes 16 of its 55), black-and-white to 5 greys and sepia to 8; the other moods cap the colours (12-16). Edits, rotations and animations of the asset keep its palette. There is no colour-count setting: Voidless picks it by size.

pose.description: Characters, front or side view: 'idle' = relaxed stance with the arms down — the default, for animation sets, rotations and almost everything. 'tpose' = arms held straight out — ONLY when the user asks for a T-pose (e.g. to rig the character in the skeleton editor). Not used for dimension 'top down', where it is left out.

prompt.description: The subject (max 300 chars; an asset sheet, type 'artwork' at size 2048 or '4k', up to 1000 so each item and its view can be named). Prefer the style/palette fields; if style is empty, a style the prompt names (e.g. 'watercolour frost mage', 'a cel-shaded golem') picks that preset and those words are taken out of the prompt, so the preset's own style words are the only ones the model sees.

referenceImage.description: Voidless+ only. Optional raw base64 image (no data: prefix) to base the result on

size.description: Output px. With model 'free' (Voidless Monarch), 16, 24, 32, 48 or 64 is the level of detail for every 2D kind (a character up to 48: its 64 is drawn at 48): drawn at that size, more detail the bigger (16 and 24 are model 'free' only). 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 192, 256 and 384 give pixel art; 512 for every other style; 768 for a sharper smooth sprite (drawn at 1024, stored at 768); 1024 for high-res (Voidless+ only, as are 2048 and '4k'). 144 is ONLY for type 'tileset' with tilesetKind 'platformer' (the side-view 3x3 sheet): nine 48 px pixel-art tiles (96 gives 32 px tiles, 192 gives 64 px). 2048 and '4k' are ASSET-SHEET sizes, only for type 'artwork' with model 'gpt-image-2.6' in a smooth (not pixel) style: 2048 = 2048x2048 (aspect '16:9': 2560x1440), '4k' = 2880x2880 (aspect '16:9': 3840x2160), kept at that size. For a set of matching assets to cut apart with extract_parts save_as 'assets'.

style.description: Style preset: pixel-art, cartoon, cel-shading, flat, hand-drawn, paper-cutout, comic-book, anime, watercolor, low-poly, 3d-render, claymation, photorealistic, voxel. Always ends up as one of these: another value is mapped to the nearest preset ('watercolour', '8-bit', 'realistic'), or the default if none fits. Empty = the preset the prompt names, at 512/1024 for non-pixel styles (at 32-384 the result is pixel art); otherwise pixel art below 512, cartoon at 512/1024.

styleAssetId.description: Voidless+ only. Optional: the id of one of your image assets whose art style to copy (its main image, full resolution). Same as passing its image key as styleImage

styleId.description: Voidless+ only. Optional: one of your saved styles (list_styles gives their ids), the same as picking it in the app. Leave styleImage and styleAssetId empty with it

styleImage.description: Voidless+ only. Optional image whose art style to copy: an image key from one of your assets (get_asset lists them, e.g. assets/64/images/<id>.png) or its cdn.voidless.dev URL. The server loads it at full resolution. Prefer this (or styleAssetId) over base64: get_image_data only returns a small thumbnail. With gpt-image-2.6 the picture itself is shown to the model; other models get a description of its style

tilesetKind.description: type 'tileset' only: 'platformer' = side-view 3x3 ground sheet (default for 2d); 'wang' = top-down two-terrain 4x5 auto-tile sheet in the free Tileset Generator's layout (default for top down; name both terrains, e.g. 'a cobblestone path in grass'), every edge matched so any arrangement tiles seamlessly; 'blob17' = top-down 17-piece sheet of one terrain on transparent. Top-down sheets have 256 px tiles; a pixel size returns pixel tiles at that size (up to 256)

type.description: 'character' = full-body sprite (uses facing/pose/bodyType); 'character portrait' = headshot; 'object' = props and items; 'artwork' = scenes/backgrounds; 'tileset' = a terrain tile sheet (always GPT-Image, see tilesetKind; below 512 it is drawn at 512 and pixelated); 'ui' = interface pieces (see uiMode).

uiMode.description: type 'ui' only: 'graphic' = button/panel/HUD piece, 'title' = game-title wordmark spelling the prompt, 'text' = plain label spelling the prompt

name: generate_image
